prompts.B:
Use case: stylized-concept. Generate ONE standalone character illustration, variant B medium coat, for a Korean personal virtual-dog project.
INPUT ROLES: image 1 is the STYLE AND DEFORMATION reference only (the small cream-and-orange crayon dog); images 2 and 3 are the actual individual dog's identity references. Do not copy the orange coat, interface, text, or background from any reference.
Match the FIRST reference's exceptionally simple, small friendly crayon doodle design closely: sparse imperfect warm charcoal pencil contours, visible dry crayon fill, cream paper left white, very few interior strokes, tiny black dot eyes and a small black rounded triangular nose, a tiny friendly mouth, small soft paws, ordinary cute seated puppy-like illustration proportions. NOT a realistic dog portrait, not elaborate pencil fur rendering. Avoid extreme chibi proportions, giant eyes, tall necks, elongated legs or sausage bodies. The reference has only a handful of strokes describing anatomy; preserve this economy.
IDENTITY from actual photos: short rounded gray floppy ears lying alongside the cheeks (never long spaniel ears), gray outer face with a WHITE central forehead blaze joining white nose bridge and full soft white muzzle/beard, dark nose, gray back/flank, white neck/bib and white lower paws. Slightly rectangular medium-build body under the stylization. Gray is soft charcoal/slate crayon with paper showing, never orange/tan. Preserve observed recognizable marking layout, don't invent new eye patches or spots. TAIL: longer dark gray feathered hair, placed low behind the haunch and trailing softly sideways near the ground, not a pointed fox tail or an upright curly tail. The low tail placement is a provisional illustration pose, not an asserted fixed anatomical tail type.
VARIANT B: MEDIUM coat, like the original standing photo: short-ish body coat, a rounded modestly fluffy white muzzle and cheeks, fluffy small white feet and a longer feathery tail. Use a FEW little curved contour tufts, not hundreds of fur hairs.
Composition: single whole dog sitting in gentle front three-quarter view, face looking towards viewer; balanced natural seated anatomy, both front paws visible, tail visible to the right behind haunch. Head about 40 percent of total character height. Dog centered and occupies about 72 percent of a square canvas with comfortable blank margins. Clean warm off-white paper background. No labels, text, hearts, props, UI, frames, multiple dogs, realism, gradients, drop shadows, glossy vector finish or pixel grid. This is a proposed appearance illustration, not an observed behavior.
prompts.A:
Edit image 1, the medium-coat gray-and-white crayon dog. Image 2 is the small original STYLE reference. Produce ONE dog only. Keep the same dog identity, the exact seated three-quarter pose, dot eyes, face direction, head/body proportions, canvas framing, warm paper background, charcoal hand-drawn contours, gray/white marking boundaries, white forehead blaze down the nose bridge, white muzzle/beard and bib, white feet, and low trailing gray feathery tail. Keep the same expression and tiny tongue. Do not invent spots, change anatomy, breed, age, eye shape or colors, or add any text/props. Retain short floppy ears beside the cheeks, no long spaniel ears. Crayon texture should stay very simple and readable at small icon size, matching image 2's sparse little doodle, not a detailed fur portrait. This is a comparative grooming/coat-length concept, not new factual evidence about the dog.
VARIANT A -- SHORT COAT. Make only the head/cheek/beard and body coat visibly shorter and neater than image 1. Use smoother compact silhouette with just a few tiny contour tufts. Compact softly rounded white muzzle still exists, white feet still soft and small. Body must not shrink in actual anatomy or become skinny. Keep long feathery tail as an identity cue; this is short head/body grooming, not tail clipping. No realistic individual hair strands, less internal white/gray strand marks. Difference should read immediately as neat short grooming while clearly the same individual and same composition.
